title: Fall and Winter Haircuts: Keeping a Little More Length
hero_alt: Man in a beanie among snow-covered trees
card_text: Cooler months, hats and a bit more on top. Cuts that carry well through winter, and the edges that stay tight all year.
lede: Fall and winter haircuts usually keep a little more length on top, so there's something to style and a bit of cover on cold mornings, while the sides, neckline and edges stay tight. A slick back, a textured crop with extra length, or a modern mullet all carry well through the cooler months. What you don't want is the whole cut drifting long, because shaggy sides and a fuzzy neckline look untidy in any season.
Here's how to adjust your cut for the colder months, a few styles that suit them, and how to live with a hat.

blocks.heading: A little more on top.
paragraphs: In the heat, shorter is easier. When the weather cools, there's less reason to keep everything short, and some extra length on top gives you more ways to wear it.
Length on top also handles hats well. Very short tops show every dent a hat leaves, while a bit more length can be pushed back into shape with your fingers.
Winter here is mild compared with much of the country, but mornings still get cold. A little more hair on top makes a real difference the moment you step outside on a chilly morning.
This isn't about growing your hair out. It's about letting the top carry a touch more for a few months.

blocks.heading: Edges don't take the winter off.
blocks.lead: The parts that make a cut look cared for.
paragraphs: Longer on top doesn't mean longer everywhere. A tidy neckline under a coat collar is what makes a cut look fresh even when the top has grown. These stay clean all year:
bullets: The neckline, with collars and scarves rubbing against it.
Around the ears, where a beanie pushes hair outward.
The sideburns and the line where hair meets beard.

blocks.heading: Three that carry well.
blocks.lead: All keep some length up top.

subsections.heading: Slick back
paragraphs: Length on top combed straight back over a short taper, like the photo above. It looks sharp with a coat collar, and it goes back into place quickly after a hat comes off.

subsections.heading: Textured crop, a bit longer
paragraphs: Keep the crop but leave extra length on top. The texture hides hat dents and still looks finished.

subsections.heading: Modern mullet
paragraphs: For people who want real length, cooler months are an easy time to let the back grow while the sides stay faded.

blocks.heading: Living with a beanie.
paragraphs: Put a hat on dry hair. Damp hair takes the hat's shape and keeps it all day.
When the hat comes off, run damp fingers through the top and push it back where it goes.
Static is another winter nuisance, especially under wool hats. A damp hand or a little product over the top usually settles it.
On a cold morning, a few warm minutes in the chair don't hurt either. The wash and scalp massage add-on is {{addon:wash-scalp-massage}} with any cut.

items.title: Essential Haircut
items.body: A longer top shaped to your style, the sides kept tight and a straight razor neck cleanup before it's styled.

items.title: Signature Cut
items.body: The same cut with the beard trimmed or lined up and a hot towel finish. A hot towel on a cold morning is hard to argue with.

items.q: What haircuts work well in winter?
items.a: Ones with a little more length on top and clean sides, like a slick back, a longer textured crop or a modern mullet.

items.q: Should I grow my hair longer in winter?
items.a: A little more on top works well for hats and styling. Keep the sides and neckline tidy either way.
They flatten them for a while. Putting the hat on dry hair and keeping some length on top helps it bounce back.

items.q: Is a mullet a good winter cut?
items.a: It's a comfortable season to grow the back while the sides stay faded.
